claims.statement: Tom Allen was declared the winner after eleven rounds against Charley Gallagher on August 17, 1869, when Gallagher's second Tom Kelley threw up the sponge.
claims.excerpt: Tom Kelley, one of Gallagher's seconds, threw up the sponge in token of defeat

claims.statement: After the fight, Allen walked to Gallagher's corner to shake hands, and Gallagher struck at him spitefully without hitting him.
claims.excerpt: Alien walked quickly over to Gallagher’s corner to shake hands with his adversary, when the latter sfruck at him spitefully, but without hitting him.

claims.statement: The referee declared the Allen-Gallagher fight a draw because he had not seen who threw up the sponge.
claims.excerpt: then the referee strangely declares the fight a draw, for the reason that he did not see who threw up the sponge

claims.statement: Tom Allen was one of Jim Elliott's seconds in Elliott's fight with Gallagher at Peach Island, near Detroit, which the crowd broke up.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen being one of Elliott’s seconds at this battle

claims.statement: Charley Gallagher was said to hold a long-standing grudge against Allen over Allen's conduct at the Elliott fight.
claims.excerpt: Gallagher long cherished an old grudge against him on account of Tom's conduct on this occasion

claims.statement: Charley Gallagher was said to have given Tom Allen a severe pounding in a rough and tumble at Cleveland.
claims.excerpt: giving Tom a severe pounding in a rough and tumble at Cléveland

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher had an unsatisfactory contest at Carroll's Island in the spring of 1869.
claims.excerpt: the unsatisfactory contest between the two at Carroll"s Is—land, last spring

claims.statement: The Allen and Mike McCoole contest resulted in no honest decision, after one side claimed a foul.
claims.excerpt: which resulted in no honest decision at all, but a miserable farce, by reason of one of the parties claiming a fictitious foul

claims.statement: The dispute over the Allen and Mike McCoole contest ended in a wrangle in the courts.
claims.excerpt: winding up in a wretched wrangle in the courts

fights.excerpt: Tom Kelley, one of Gallagher's seconds, threw up the sponge in token of defeat
fights.notes: Editorial's account: Allen won. The referee declared a draw, which the editorial criticises.

fights.excerpt: the unsatisfactory contest between the two at Carroll"s Is—land, last spring
fights.notes: 'Last spring' (1869). Described as unsatisfactory; no result given. May be the same as the February 1869 fight that other articles report as a two-round loss for Allen.

fights.excerpt: giving Tom a severe pounding in a rough and tumble at Cléveland
fights.notes: Rough and tumble with no rounds or stakes given; date not given.

fights.excerpt: which resulted in no honest decision at all, but a miserable farce, by reason of one of the parties claiming a fictitious foul
fights.notes: Date not given in this article (June 1869 per other articles). Editorial says no honest decision was reached.

notes: Editorial, not news: its account of Allen's win is the paper's view. Several entries are hearsay or recollection.
